(1:22)Rob Dawson and James OlleyApr 17, 2026, 10:00 AM ETReactionsWe still have a month to go in the 2025-26 season of the Premier League, but it feels like Arsenal's visit to Manchester City on Sunday will be the match that decides the destination of the title.Mikel Arteta's Arsenal have been top of the table since September as they bid to become champions of England for the first time since 2004, but City boss Pep Guardiola has pipped the team coached by his former assistant to the title twice in the last three years and his team remains close behind as we enter the home stretch this term.Who will prevail at the Etihad Stadium? And how will the result affect the title race? ESPN's Rob Dawson and James Olley run through the key points ahead of this crucial showdown.- Ranked: Who are the top 50 players in the Premier League right now? - Is it happening again? Arsenal title-race stumble follows familiar pattern - Pep up your wardrobe with Man City's Guardiola-branded clothing rangeWhat's at stake in this game in terms of the title race?Sunday's meeting is the closest thing you can get to title decider in mid-April. City have the momentum, Arsenal have the points on the board. City have the pedigree from winning six of the last eight league titles, Arsenal have the relentless hunger of trying to end a 22-year drought. The irresistible force of City's attack -- featuring Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Jérémy Doku -- meets the immovable object of the best defence in the league, with Gabriel Magalhães and William Saliba among the best centre-back pairings the Premier League has seen. Something has to give.Victory for City will move them within three points, and three days later they play their game in hand against relegation-battling Burnley. They could be top by then. That would leave Arsenal with a firm sense the trophy is slipping from their grasp. Conversely, a win for the Gunners would be transformative: nine points clear, City's pride severely damaged and the title solely in their hands with just five games to play. A draw would leave Arsenal in the box seat but City still with an outside chance.Matches are often victims of excessive hyperbole. This one isn't. -- James OlleyWhat happened in their previous meetings this season?City and Arsenal have met twice already this season, registering one draw and one City win. September's 1-1 draw at the Emirates in the League was notable for an apparent change in Guardiola's usual tactics. Not one for being overly defensive, it looked like the City boss had instructed his team to 'park the bus' and wait for opportunities to counter-attack. It almost worked; after Haaland's early goal, Arsenal only salvaged a point thanks to Gabriel Martinelli's 93rd-minute equaliser.The Carabao Cup final at Wembley last month was more significant. City arrived on the back of a morale-denting UEFA Champions League exit to Real Madrid, while Arsenal were on the back of a 14-match unbeaten run stretching back to January. With the first trophy of the season on the line, the first half was tight and cagey. But while Arsenal adopted the same approach after half-time, Guardiola tweaked his game plan and City took control. Two goals from break-out England star Nico O'Reilly -- the day after celebrating his 21st birthday -- earned City a 2-0 win.The respective form of the two teams since could not be more different. City have recorded comprehensive wins over Liverpool and Chelsea, scoring seven and conceding none. Arsenal, meanwhile, have played four and won just once. Ahead of Sunday's meeting, one team is full of confidence and playing well and the other is not. -- Rob DawsonWhat to watch for on each teamManchester City: Guardiola will know that Arsenal are vulnerable and he will look to take advantage. At least from the outside, it feels similar to Arsenal's visit to the Etihad in April 2023. Arsenal kicked off in that game five points clear of City at the top of the table. But what was billed beforehand as a potential title-decider very quickly turned into a mauling. Arsenal were dealing with injuries and fatigue, and City made them pay. The opening to the game was so frantic and ferocious that Arsenal couldn't cope. City went 1-0 up inside the first 10 minutes and scored again before half-time. It ended 4-1 and left Guardiola's team two points behind with two games in hand. City went on to win their third consecutive title by five points.The way the two teams are playing heading into Sunday, it's easy to see the same thing happening this time. Haaland looks sharp again after a slow start to 2026 and Cherki is one of the most in-form players in the league. Arsenal aren't scoring freely at the moment and they face a monumental task to keep those two, plus Antoine Semenyo and Doku, quiet at the other end. -- DawsonArsenal: Arteta treats City with more respect than anyone else. Part of that is his admiration for long-time friend and former colleague Guardiola, as well as an acknowledgment that City have been the most consistently devastating team for the last decade.As Arsenal have steadily closed the gap, however, that conservatism has led to some frustration that Arteta has not shown more attacking intent in this fixture. Two years ago, they arrived at the end of March and played out a 0-0 draw. Last season, they were 2-1 up before having Leandro Trossard sent off on the stroke of half-time. The Gunners did not even try to attack in the second half, with Arteta suggesting afterwards there was simply no other way of approaching the situation.What does he do this time? Arsenal are not defending with the intensity and cohesion of earlier in the season, and merely trying to play for a draw here would only ramp up the criticism that Arsenal's style is too cautious to actually win silverware. But opening up too much risks giving City's in-form attacking players the space to define the game. It is a delicate balancing act but the level of intent Arsenal show will be heavily scrutinised with many believing now is the time for the Gunners to seize their moment and win a game of this magnitude. If they do, they have one hand firmly on the trophy. -- OlleyKey clashesGianluigi Donnarumma vs. Gabriel: This is a left-field choice given they won't be near each other very often, but it's a game that could be decided by City's goalkeeper and the Arsenal defender. The Gunners' big threat is from set-pieces -- particularly if they're not creating much from open play. Gabriel is an expert in those situations, and the onus will be on Donnarumma to deal with the danger.If the giant Italy No. 1 can command his penalty area -- punching or catching balls swung into the box from free kicks and corners -- then a large part of Arsenal's threat will be nullified. If Arsenal don't score, then City will win. If, on the other hand, Arsenal can make the most of their set-pieces and Gabriel is allowed to cause chaos in City's penalty area, then Arsenal will have a good chance of edging a fixture which could be decided by very fine margins. -- DawsonDeclan Rice vs. Rodri: Rodri has struggled to consistently reproduce his best form since returning from a serious knee injury but his Carabao Cup final performance -- particularly in the second half -- was a masterclass. The 29-year-old remains pivotal to establishing the control City need in games to produce their best, and Rodri helped overwhelm Rice and Martín Zubimendi at Wembley.Rice defied all expectations to play in the second leg of Arsenal's Champions League quarterfinal against Sporting CP by overcoming illness to play the entire 90 minutes. The England international assumed the captaincy, too -- keep an eye on if he retains that at Etihad Stadium as another sign of his growing importance. But if there is one lingering doubt about Rice, it is his ability to dictate and decide games of this magnitude on a regular basis. There have also been signs of fatigue after another gruelling campaign, but Rice has a phenomenal capacity to absorb that workload. Getting the better of Rodri on Sunday would go a long way to securing the win -- and the title -- he craves. -- Olleyplay0:36Guardiola: Title race 'over' if Arsenal beat Manchester CityPep Guardiola looks ahead to a huge clash in the Premier League title race as Manchester City host Arsenal.What the managers sayPep Guardiola, Manchester City:"If we lose, it's over."They are so strong in all departments. Duals, physicality, if you allow them to make a good process by not being aggressive they make a good build-up."That's why they are who they are. Top of the Premier League all season and that's why I'm proud to be there and challenging them."Mikel Arteta, Arsenal:"I'm not going to spend one second talking about that [playing for a draw]. We prepare every game to win, that's why we are where we are and we're going to continue to do the same."We have earned the right to be in this position, to be challenging and with the possibility to win and the opportunity to win on Sunday, arguably against the best team and the best manager that this league has ever seen."That's a huge privilege, and we can't wait to play the game, and we're going to prepare the game to win it, that's for sure, and we see that as a big opportunity for us."play0:38Arteta never got clarification on Haaland's 'stay humble' commentMikel Arteta reveals he hasn't spoken to Erling Haaland about when the striker told him to "stay humble."PredictionsMan City 3-1 Arsenal: The Gunners haven't dealt well with the psychological punch of losing the Carabao Cup final. Damage-limitation mode is unlikely to work for long at the Etihad and everything points to a City win. -- DawsonMan City 2-0 Arsenal: City have the momentum, a clear week of preparation and home advantage in their favour. Arsenal can make it difficult for a while, but City possess the in-form individual quality to edge it. -- Olley Rosenior was out of his depth at Chelsea, and it was obvious from the startplayThe damning stats of Liam Rosenior's time at Chelsea (0:51)Liam Rosenior's tenure as Chelsea head coach has set a few unwanted club records. (0:51)Mark OgdenApr 22, 2026, 02:30 PM ETCloseMark Ogden is a senior soccer writer for ESPN.com. Read his archive here and follow him on Twitter: @MarkOgden_.ReactionsLiam Rosenior lasted just 106 days as Chelsea head coach, but it was obvious on Day 2 that the 41-year-old was ill-equipped for the job he had been hired to do.In truth, it was also clear on Day 1 considering his lack of top-level coaching experience and the naïve belief of BlueCo, Chelsea's owner, that Rosenior could make the transition from coaching partner club Strasbourg to leading a dressing room of big-name players at Stamford Bridge following Enzo Maresca's dismissal.More than 24 hours after watching training on his first day in charge, though, Rosenior chose not to be involved with team selection or play any part on the bench as his new side suffered a 2-1 defeat away to local rivals Fulham in his second day in the job, opting instead to take a more detached approach, sitting alongside Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali in the stand at Craven Cottage.It was the first of many mistakes by Rosenior. Others would be more obvious and embarrassing: the bizarre claim that his players were "respecting the ball" while surrounding referee Paul Tierney in a prematch huddle, his odd boast that he was "managing the school team when I was 11" and the decision to hand Alejandro Garnacho a tactical note in the 85th minute of an 8-2 aggregate defeat against Paris Saint-Germain.All of Rosenior's gaffes and his corporate speak of "alignment" and "process" combined to make him a figure of ridicule, with some former teammates mocking his unrecognizable persona. Sources told ESPN that Rosenior was so hurt by some of the criticism that he privately challenged his detractors, with one admitting to being surprised that the Chelsea coach was allowing himself to be distracted by the noise.But why did that first misstep at Fulham matter? It mattered because it highlighted Rosenior's inexperience and inability to realize that when you are Chelsea coach, walking in the footsteps of José Mourinho, Carlo Ancelotti, Antonio Conte and Thomas Tuchel, everything that you say or do is noticed and judged to an extent way beyond anything he had lived through previously in his career.Having walked into a job after his predecessor had failed to win any of his final four games, a more seasoned coach or manager would have taken a grip of the situation by attempting to make an instant impact, showing skeptical players and supporters that he had the skill set and personality that the Chelsea job demands. Instead, Rosenior sat it out as the supporters chanted angry songs about the owners.He projected an air of thinking he knew what he was doing, without convincing anyone that he did. Three months later, after a run of seven defeats in eight games and five straight Premier League defeats without scoring that led to Rosenior's dismissal, it would be difficult to argue that the players were convinced by their unproven young coach.Under Rosenior, Chelsea failed to win against any of their traditional Big Six rivals or fellow European heavyweights. He suffered three defeats against Arsenal, that humbling UEFA Champions League loss to PSG, and his side were also beaten by Manchester City and Manchester United.There was also the decision to hit Enzo Fernández with an internal two-match suspension for talking up the prospects of a move to Real Madrid, but despite Marc Cucurella making similar positive noises about Barcelona as well as questioning the decision to fire Maresca, the Spain defender escaped any punishment.Rosenior spoke about how the Fernández ban had been a "club decision," hinting at it being taken by senior figures above him, which only served to undermine him once again in the eyes of the players and supporters. The structure that Rosenior had happily agreed to work within was ultimately the reason why he was never likely to succeed.BlueCo's vision, driven by sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Laurence Stewart, is of the head coach merely being a cog in a bigger wheel.It is why Chelsea's past two hires -- Maresca and Rosenior -- were plucked from relative obscurity to fit into the club's ecosystem. After winning two trophies and qualifying for the Champions League in his first season in charge, Maresca wanted a greater say in recruitment, so he was quickly dispensed with once he spoke out to criticize the BlueCo model.Rosenior was never likely to be as abrasive as Maresca, but while that might have suited the club, it rankled with supporters who viewed him as a "yes man."The players also knew that he was not the boss, but a man hired by many bosses above him. Those same bosses are now likely to be under greater scrutiny from the owners after their disastrous decision to appoint Rosenior.Sources have said that the failed experiment, which leaves Chelsea facing a failure to qualify for the Champions League, might prompt a rethink at the highest level about the BlueCo model and that a more experienced coach is now required. Xabi Alonso, Cesc Fàbregas and Andoni Iraola are likely to be considered, while Frank Lampard -- who has two previous spells as Chelsea coach -- could also be a contender after guiding Coventry City to promotion to the Premier League.Having diminished the role of head coach by hiring Rosenior when he was clearly out of his depth, though, Chelsea have a credibility problem of their own making.Rosenior failed because he wasn't up to it, but the people who hired him are arguably even more culpable than the man who lasted just 106 days. Pep says Man City can 'handle' stress of Arsenal title raceRob DawsonApr 22, 2026, 06:47 PM ETReactionsPep Guardiola said he's sure Manchester City can handle the pressure of a tight title race after a nervous night against Burnley.City won 1-0 at Turf Moor on Wednesday to go top of the Premier League table ahead of Arsenal on goal difference and relegate Burnley in the process.There were some tense moments for Guardiola's team -- particularly when goalkeeper Martin Dúbravka came up for a stoppage-time corner -- but it got over the line."I don't have a machine or something like that. How was your pressure today? How do you feel? Were you nervous or not nervous?" said Guardiola."I don't know, but I'm pretty sure that this, for the future, for all of them, for all of us, in this club will be good, as much you experience, as much as you've been there many times, you handle it better."But in general, in the way we play it was really, really, really good. So, the commitment, the way, how many plays arrive, and we just missed a little bit that moment."It looked like City might be able to boost their goal difference when Erling Haaland opened the scoring after just five minutes.But they were wasteful after that and ended the night with 28 shots and an xG of 3.5 with only one goal to show for it."I think we played really, really good," said Guardiola. "I didn't see all the images and the chances that we had, but I had a feeling that we had a lot."And just for many of these types of games, we score the second on the third, for the chances that we create, we deserve it."Arsenal has the chance to restore their lead in the Premier League this weekend against Newcastle, while City take part in the FA Cup semifinals against Southampton. (0:32)Sam Marsden and Moises LlorensApr 22, 2026, 06:55 PM ETReactionsLamine Yamal has handed Barcelona and Spain a major injury worry after being forced off immediately after scoring a penalty in Barça's LaLiga win over Celta Vigo on Wednesday.Club sources told ESPN the initial indication is that he has a torn hamstring, but the severity of the tear and the length of time Yamal could be sidelined will be confirmed via scans Thursday, once the swelling has gone down.- Bayern, Germany star Gnabry to miss World Cup - Neymar, Barça cleared in Santos transfer caseIf that is the case, Yamal could sit out the rest of the season with Barça, with attention then turning to this summer's World Cup, where he was set to be the key player for European champions Spain."We have to wait," Barça coach Hansi Flick said after the game. "We have to see what it is. There is something. He felt it. After the goal, he would not leave the pitch without reason."So it's something. Something happened. Hopefully it's not so bad, but we have to wait until tomorrow."Yamal won and converted a spot kick to give Barça the lead in the 40th minute, but rather than celebrate the goal, he immediately dropped to the ground and called for the medical staff.Replays showed the 18-year-old grabbing his hamstring after scoring the penalty that proved enough to give Barcelona a victory.After receiving treatment on the pitch for a few minutes, he was able to walk off, but he was not able to continue. Roony Bardghji replaced him just before halftime.Yamal is set to make his World Cup debut with Spain against Cape Verde on June 15."Hopefully Lamine will only miss a few weeks," Barcelona midfielder Pedri said. "I wish him the best of luck. He needs to remain calm because he's young and will surely recover well."play1:12Barcelona vs. Celta Vigo - Game HighlightsWatch the Game Highlights from Barcelona vs. Celta Vigo, 04/22/2026Barcelona also lost Portugal defender João Cancelo because of an apparent muscle injury to his right leg in the 24th minute."We hope their injuries are not serious and that they are back with us as soon as possible," Barcelona goalkeeper Joan García said.Barça can ill afford to be without Yamal for any stretch of time as they attempt to get over the line in LaLiga.Wednesday's 1-0 victory took Barcelona nine points clear of second-place Real Madrid with six games left.Barça and Madrid still have to play each other, with the two rivals meeting in the second LaLiga Clásico of the season at Camp Nou on May 10.Yamal has struggled with a sports hernia at times this season but has not sat out many games because of that or other injuries, making 45 appearances in all competitions.Wednesday's goal took his tally for the campaign to 24, and he also has 17 assists.
